notes: Evidence base for get_evidence (CONCEPT §7.7). Only entries with verified=true may be
quoted by the agent or the proposal; verified=false means the figure has not been read
back to its source yet and must not be presented as evidence.
`metric` is load-bearing, not decoration. Several sources report ROOF SURFACE or INDOOR
temperature drops of 11-13 degC, which are an order of magnitude larger than any
neighbourhood LST effect. Presenting those as area cooling would overstate what TEDUH can
deliver by roughly 10x, so every metric string names what was measured and where.

metrics.lst_change_c: Satellite land surface temperature over an area. Directly comparable to TEDUH model output.
metrics.air_temp_change_c: Ambient air temperature. NOT comparable to LST; always smaller.
metrics.roof_surface_temp_change_c: Temperature of the roof skin itself. NOT area cooling.
metrics.indoor_temp_change_c: Temperature inside the building under the roof. NOT area cooling.
metrics.heat_flux_reduction_pct: Conductive heat gain through the roof assembly.
metrics.energy_saving_pct: Cooling energy consumption of the building.

evidence.context: Kuala Lumpur, tropical megacity. Random forest on Landsat 8 indices, scenario of +25% NDVI citywide. Model KGE 0.68, spatial bias +/-1.6 degC.
evidence.source_title: Machine Learning in Modeling Urban Heat Islands: A Data-Driven Approach for Kuala Lumpur
evidence.source_authors: Miniandi, N. D.; Jamal, M. H.; Muhammad, M. K. I.; Sharrar, L.; Shahid, S.
evidence.verification_note: Read back to the abstract: 'an improvement in NDVI by 25% can cause a drop in LST ranging from -1.4 to 0.1 degC'. Exactly as CONCEPT §7.7 recorded it.
evidence.relevance_note: Closest published analogue to TEDUH: same intervention, same metric (LST), tropical Southeast Asian megacity, comparable ML-scenario method. The paper also reports cooling is LARGEST where LST is already highest, which independently supports prioritising the hottest kelurahan. Note the upper bound is +0.1 degC: greening does not cool every cell.

evidence.context: Kuala Lumpur. Same model and paper as ev_ndvi_kl_2025, scenario of +25% albedo citywide.
evidence.source_title: Machine Learning in Modeling Urban Heat Islands: A Data-Driven Approach for Kuala Lumpur
evidence.source_authors: Miniandi, N. D.; Jamal, M. H.; Muhammad, M. K. I.; Sharrar, L.; Shahid, S.
evidence.verification_note: Abstract: 'a 25% increase in albedo can decrease the LST by -1.2 to 0.1 degC'. Exactly as CONCEPT §7.7 recorded it.
evidence.relevance_note: This is the AREA-scale albedo figure and the right comparator for TEDUH's cool_roof scenario output. Do not mix it with the roof-skin figures below.

evidence.context: Indonesia, tropical. Single-storey building, pitched roof modified into a cool roof. Measured on the roof and indoors, NOT over an area.
evidence.source_title: A Comparative Study of Cool Roof and Green Roof Performance in Tropical Area of Indonesia
evidence.source_journal: Journal of Architectural Research and Design Studies (JARDS), Universitas Islam Indonesia
evidence.verification_note: Confirmed: temperature reduction up to 11.58 degC, heat flux up to -95%, energy saving up to 55%. CONCEPT §7.7 records the energy range as '36-55%'; only the 55% upper bound is confirmed, the 36% lower bound is NOT and must not be quoted.
evidence.relevance_note: BUILDING-SCALE, not area-scale. Use for a homeowner answer in Cek Atap, never to describe kelurahan cooling. The paper finds cool roof better for NIGHT-TIME thermal comfort and suited to pitched/tiled roofs, which matches the recommend_roof_action rule in CONCEPT §8.5.

evidence.context: Indonesia, tropical. Single-storey building, flat roof with vegetation. Measured on the roof and indoors, NOT over an area.
evidence.source_title: A Comparative Study of Cool Roof and Green Roof Performance in Tropical Area of Indonesia
evidence.source_journal: Journal of Architectural Research and Design Studies (JARDS), Universitas Islam Indonesia
evidence.verification_note: Confirmed: temperature reduction up to 13.14 degC, heat flux up to -91%, energy saving about 60%.
evidence.relevance_note: BUILDING-SCALE, not area-scale. The paper finds green roof better at cutting DAYTIME indoor heat gain and suited to flat concrete roofs, so a mostly daytime-occupied building saves more energy with green roof than cool roof. Matches the flat/concrete_slab branch of recommend_roof_action (CONCEPT §8.5).

evidence.context: Southeast Asia review. Road surface itself reported at -9 degC or more; the -0.5 to -1.0 degC here is the surrounding UHI effect.
evidence.source_title: Belum terlacak - notebook menyebut 'SNTI 2026' dan 'ICES 2025 (review Asia Tenggara)'
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI. Neither proceedings reference is specific enough to locate: no author, no title, and SNTI 2026 postdates this work. Do not quote. P1 only -- cool pavement is outside the M1-M7 scope.

evidence.context: Meta-review of urban greening; location and climate not recorded.
evidence.source_title: Belum terlacak - notebook hanya menyebut 'review dalam notebook'
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI dan patut dicurigai. A 1.5-4.5 degC AIR temperature drop from greening sits far above the peer-reviewed area-scale results (cf. ev_ndvi_kl_2025 at -1.4 degC for LST, and air effects are normally SMALLER than surface effects). Likely a best-case or park-interior measurement presented as a general range. Do not quote until the primary source is found.

evidence.context: Tokyo. Climbing vegetation screening a window or wall; also reported to cut about 80% of incoming sunlight.
evidence.source_title: The Use of Greenery to Combat Urban Warming in Tokyo
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI. The title is known but the publication was not located. Temperate climate, so transferability to Jakarta is unclear regardless. Useful for the asbestos-roof safe-option branch of recommend_roof_action, but only once sourced.

evidence.context: Singapore, Cooling Singapore / Digital Urban Climate Twin (DUCT). Coordinated multi-intervention package, reported at hotspots rather than citywide.
evidence.source_title: Cooling Singapore - Digital Urban Climate Twin (DUCT)
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI. The programme is real and well documented, but this -7 degC hotspot figure and the -8% cooling-energy figure need pinning to a named report. It is a HOTSPOT maximum, not an area mean, so quoting it as typical would mislead.

evidence.context: Melbourne urban forest strategy. The 5-10-20 rule: at most 5% of the urban forest from one species, 10% from one genus, 20% from one family.
evidence.source_title: Urban Forest Diversity Guidelines (City of Melbourne)
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI as a citation, though the 5-10-20 rule itself is widely used in urban forestry. Carries no numeric risk since it makes no temperature claim; it belongs in brief guidance on pest and disease resilience, never in a cooling estimate.

evidence.context: Bandung, Indonesia. Pterocarpus indicus (angsana), Swietenia macrophylla (mahoni), Samanea saman (trembesi) reported to give significant cooling.
evidence.source_title: Belum terlacak - notebook menyebut studi Bandung tanpa sitasi
evidence.verification_note: TIDAK TERVERIFIKASI. The three species are standard Indonesian shade trees and plausible, but 'significant cooling' has no number attached and no source. Worth tracing: a sourced local species list would be directly useful for planting guidance, and could also let canopy_m2_per_tree in config/costs.yaml stop being an assumption.
